work: Sirat Rasul Allah / The Life of Muhammad
author: Ibn Ishaq (d. 767), ed. Ibn Hisham
ref: Guillaume p. 363 'The affair of the B. Qaynuqa'' (bracketed (568))
english: 'Asim b. 'Umar b. Qatada said that the B. Qaynuqa' were the first of the Jews to break their agreement with the apostle and to go to war, between Badr and Uhud (568), and the apostle besieged them until they surrendered unconditionally.
translator: A. Guillaume, The Life of Muhammad (OUP, Karachi; 1955 edition; PDF copy 2010 Adobe scan)
what_it_says: Ibn Ishaq's source ('Asim b. 'Umar b. Qatada) says Qaynuqa' broke their agreement and went to war between Badr and Uhud; the Prophet besieged them until unconditional surrender.

work: Sirat Rasul Allah / The Life of Muhammad
author: Ibn Ishaq (d. 767), ed. Ibn Hisham
ref: Guillaume p. 363 'Abdullah b. Ubayy intercession; bracketed (569), (570)
english: 'Abdullah b. Ubayy b. Salul went to him when God had put them in his power and said, '0 Muhammad, deal kindly with my clients' (now they were allies of Khazraj), but the apostle put him off. He repeated the words, and the apostle turned away from him, whereupon he thrust his hand into the collar of the apostle's robe (569); the apostle was so angry that his face became almost black. ... 'You can have them (570).'
translator: A. Guillaume, The Life of Muhammad (OUP, Karachi; 1955 edition; PDF copy 2010 Adobe scan)
what_it_says: Ibn Ubayy intercedes for the Qaynuqa' (his clients) and the Prophet finally grants them to him ('You can have them'); the sira records the Prophet's anger.

work: Sirat Rasul Allah / The Life of Muhammad
author: Ibn Ishaq (d. 767), ed. Ibn Hisham
ref: Guillaume p. 437 'The deportation of the B. al-Nadir, A.H.4'; bracketed (679), (680)
english: The apostle ordered them to prepare for war and to march against them (679)' Then he went off with the men until he came upon them (680). The Jews took refuge in their forts and the apostle ordered that the palm-trees should be cut down and burnt
translator: A. Guillaume, The Life of Muhammad (OUP, Karachi; 1955 edition; PDF copy 2010 Adobe scan)
what_it_says: After a plot to drop a rock on him at Nadir (as the sira tells it), the Prophet marches against the Nadir, who retreat to their forts; he orders their palm trees cut down and burnt.

work: Sirat Rasul Allah / The Life of Muhammad
author: Ibn Ishaq (d. 767), ed. Ibn Hisham
ref: Guillaume p. 437 (the rock-plot story) and footnote 1 on p. 437 (Guillaume's note: 'another and later story has been attached')
english: [Narrative] 'Amr b. Jihash b. Ka'b volunteered to do this and went up to throw down a rock. As the apostle was with a number of his companions among whom were Abu Bakr, 'Umar, and 'Ali, news came to him from heaven about what these people intended, so he got up and said to his companions, 'Don't go away until I come to you' ... [Guillaume's note] I think it is clear that another and later story has been attached to this incident. Obviously if the prophet had overheard their designs there was no need of a supernatural communication from heaven.
translator: A. Guillaume, The Life of Muhammad (OUP, Karachi; 1955 edition; PDF copy 2010 Adobe scan)
what_it_says: The sira's justification for the Nadir war is an alleged assassination plot; Guillaume doubts the 'heavenly news' version and thinks a later story was attached.

work: Sirat Rasul Allah / The Life of Muhammad
author: Ibn Ishaq (d. 767), ed. Ibn Hisham
ref: Guillaume pp. 437-438 (deportation terms; Sura of Exile, Q 59:2); bracketed (681)-(682)
english: They asked the apostle to deport them and to spare their lives on condition that they could retain all their property which they could carry on camels, except their armour, and he agreed. So they loaded their camels with what they could carry. ... Some went to Khaybar and others went to Syria. [p.438] They left their property to the apostle and it became his personal property which he could dispose of as he wished. He divided it among the first emigrants to the exclusion of the Ansar, except that Sahl b. Hunayf and Abu Dujana Simak b. Kharasha complained of poverty and so he gave them some.
translator: A. Guillaume, The Life of Muhammad (OUP, Karachi; 1955 edition; PDF copy 2010 Adobe scan)
what_it_says: The Nadir negotiated deportation with the right to take goods on camels (except armour); their land and property passed to the Prophet and were given to the Emigrants, not the Ansar.

work: Sirat Rasul Allah / The Life of Muhammad
author: Ibn Ishaq (d. 767), ed. Ibn Hisham
ref: Guillaume p. 460 (Abu Sufyan's speech during the Trench, 'the B. Qurana have broken their word to us')
english: Abu Sufyan got up and said, "O Quraysh, let every man see who is sitting next him." ... Then Abu Sufyan said: no Quraysh, we are not in a permanent camp; the horses and camels are dying; the B. Qurana have broken their word to us and we have heard disquieting reports of them.
translator: A. Guillaume, The Life of Muhammad (OUP, Karachi; 1955 edition; PDF copy 2010 Adobe scan)
what_it_says: During the Trench, Abu Sufyan tells Quraysh that Banu Qurayza have broken their word to them, a treaty-breach claim that the sira puts into the enemy's mouth.

work: Sirat Rasul Allah / The Life of Muhammad
author: Ibn Ishaq (d. 767), ed. Ibn Hisham
ref: Guillaume p. 461 'The raid on B. Quraiza'; bracketed (705), (706)
english: According to what al-Zuhri told me, at the time of the noon prayers Gabriel came to the apostle ... He asked the apostle if he had abandoned fighting, and when he said that he had he said that the angels had not yet laid aside their arms ... 'God commands you, Muhammad, to go to B. Quraiza. I am about to go to them to shake their stronghold.' ... The apostle besieged them for twenty-five nights until they were sore pressed and God cast terror into their hearts.
translator: A. Guillaume, The Life of Muhammad (OUP, Karachi; 1955 edition; PDF copy 2010 Adobe scan)
what_it_says: The sira has Gabriel order the march on Qurayza right after the Trench; the Prophet besieged them for twenty-five nights.

work: Sirat Rasul Allah / The Life of Muhammad
author: Ibn Ishaq (d. 767), ed. Ibn Hisham
ref: Guillaume pp. 462-463 (Ka'b b. Asad's three options; bracketed (686)-(688))
english: Ka'b b. Asad said to them: 'O Jews, you can see what has happened to you; I offer you three alternatives. ... (i) We will follow this man ... (ii) let us kill our wives and children and send men with their swords drawn to Muhammad ... (iii) tonight is the eve of the sabbath ...' They said, 'We will never abandon the laws of the Torah and never change it for another.' ... They said, 'Should we kill these poor creatures? What would be the good of life when they were dead?'
translator: A. Guillaume, The Life of Muhammad (OUP, Karachi; 1955 edition; PDF copy 2010 Adobe scan)
what_it_says: Ka'b b. Asad offers three options before the surrender; the Qurayza reject conversion and refuse to kill their families; Ka'b's third proposal is a night attack on the Sabbath eve, which the sira has them refuse.

work: Sirat Rasul Allah / The Life of Muhammad
author: Ibn Ishaq (d. 767), ed. Ibn Hisham
ref: Guillaume p. 464 (Sa'd's judgement, the executions); bracketed (709); margin 690 (verified on page image)
english: Sa'd asked, 'Do you covenant by Allah that you accept the judgement I pronounce on them?' They said Yes ... Then I give judgement that the men should be killed, the property divided, and the women and children taken as captives. ... Then he sent for them and struck off their heads in those trenches as they were brought out to him in batches. ... There were 600 or 700 in all, though some put the figure as high as 800 or 900.
translator: A. Guillaume, The Life of Muhammad (OUP, Karachi; 1955 edition; PDF copy 2010 Adobe scan)
page: p. 464 (bracketed (709); margin 690; image-checked on PDF page 256)
what_it_says: Sa'd's judgement is carried out: the men are killed in trenches dug in the Medina market in batches, and the sira gives a total of 600-700 (or up to 800-900).

work: Sahih al-Bukhari
author: Muhammad al-Bukhari (d. 870)
ref: Bukhari 4122 (sunnah.com numbering; in-book Book 64 (Maghazi), Hadith 166)
arabic: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ فَأَيْنَ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَأَشَارَ إِلَى بَنِي قُرَيْظَةَ، فَأَتَاهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَنَزَلُوا عَلَى حُكْمِهِ، فَرَدَّ الْحُكْمَ إِلَى سَعْدٍ، قَالَ فَإِنِّي أَحْكُمُ فِيهِمْ أَنْ تُقْتَلَ الْمُقَاتِلَةُ، وَأَنْ تُسْبَى النِّسَاءُ وَالذُّرِّيَّةُ، وَأَنْ تُقْسَمَ أَمْوَالُهُمْ‏.‏ قَالَ هِشَامٌ فَأَخْبَرَنِي أَبِي عَنْ عَائِشَةَ أَنَّ سَعْدًا قَالَ اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّكَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُ لَيْسَ أَحَدٌ أَحَبَّ إِلَىَّ أَنْ أُجَاهِدَهُمْ فِيكَ مِنْ قَوْمٍ كَذَّبُوا رَسُولَكَ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَأَخْرَجُوهُ، اللَّهُمَّ فَإِنِّي أَظُنُّ أَنَّكَ قَدْ وَضَعْتَ الْحَرْبَ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَهُمْ، فَإِنْ كَانَ بَقِيَ مِنْ حَرْبِ قُرَيْشٍ شَىْءٌ، فَأَبْقِنِي لَهُ حَتَّى أُجَاهِدَهُمْ فِيكَ، وَإِنْ كُنْتَ وَضَعْتَ الْحَرْبَ فَافْجُرْهَا، وَاجْعَلْ مَوْتَتِي فِيهَا‏.‏ فَانْفَجَرَتْ مِنْ لَبَّتِهِ، فَلَمْ يَرُعْهُمْ وَفِي الْمَسْجِدِ خَيْمَةٌ مِنْ بَنِي

english: Narrated `Aisha:Sa`d was wounded on the day of Khandaq (i.e. Trench) when a man from Quraish, called Hibban bin Al-`Araqa hit him (with an arrow). The man was Hibban bin Qais from (the tribe of) Bani Mais bin 'Amir bin Lu'ai who shot an arrow at Sa`d's medial arm vein (or main artery of the arm). The Prophet (ﷺ) pitched a tent (for Sa`d) in the Mosque so that he might be near to the Prophet (ﷺ) to visit. When the Prophet returned from the (battle) of Al-Khandaq (i.e. Trench) and laid down his arms and took a bath Gabriel came to him while he (i.e. Gabriel) was shaking the dust off his head, and said, "You have laid down the arms?" By Allah, I have not laid them down. Go out to them (to attack them)." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Where?" Gabriel pointed towards Bani Quraiza. So Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) went to them (i.e. Banu Quraiza) (i.e. besieged them). They then surrendered to the Prophet's judgment but he directed them to Sa`d to give his verdict concerning them. Sa`d said, "I give my judgment that their warriors should be killed, their women and children should be taken as captives, and their properties distributed." Narrated Hisham: My father informed me that `Aisha said, "Sa`d said, "O Allah! And if there still remains any fight with the Quraish (infidels), then keep me alive till I fight against them for Your Sake. But if you have brought the war to an end, then let this wound burst and cause my death thereby.' So blood gushed from the wound. There was a tent in the Mosque belonging to Banu Ghifar who were surprised by the blood flowing towards them . They said, 'O people of the tent! work: Sahih al-Bukhari
author: Muhammad al-Bukhari (d. 870)
ref: Bukhari 3043 (Book 56 (Jihad), Hadith 249)
arabic: حَدَّثَنَا سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ حَرْبٍ، حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ أَبِي أُمَامَةَ ـ هُوَ ابْنُ سَهْلِ بْنِ حُنَيْفٍ ـ عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيِّ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ قَالَ لَمَّا نَزَلَتْ بَنُو قُرَيْظَةَ عَلَى حُكْمِ سَعْدٍ ـ هُوَ ابْنُ مُعَاذٍ ـ بَعَثَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم، وَكَانَ قَرِيبًا مِنْهُ، فَجَاءَ عَلَى حِمَارٍ، فَلَمَّا دَنَا قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ قُومُوا إِلَى سَيِّدِكُمْ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَجَاءَ فَجَلَسَ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ لَهُ ‏"‏ إِنَّ هَؤُلاَءِ نَزَلُوا عَلَى حُكْمِكَ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ فَإِنِّي أَحْكُمُ أَنْ تُقْتَلَ الْمُقَاتِلَةُ، وَأَنْ تُسْبَى الذُّرِّيَّةُ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ لَقَدْ حَكَمْتَ فِيهِمْ بِحُكْمِ الْمَلِكِ ‏"‏‏.‏

work: Sahih al-Bukhari
author: Muhammad al-Bukhari (d. 870)
ref: Bukhari 371 (Book 8 (Prayers), Hadith 23; the Fajr at Khaybar)
arabic: فَخِذَ نَبِيِّ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم، ثُمَّ حَسَرَ الإِزَارَ عَنْ فَخِذِهِ حَتَّى إِنِّي أَنْظُرُ إِلَى بَيَاضِ فَخِذِ نَبِيِّ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَلَمَّا دَخَلَ الْقَرْيَةَ قَالَ ‏"‏ اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، خَرِبَتْ خَيْبَرُ، إِنَّا إِذَا نَزَلْنَا بِسَاحَةِ قَوْمٍ فَسَاءَ صَبَاحُ الْمُنْذَرِينَ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَهَا ثَلاَثًا‏.‏ قَالَ وَخَرَجَ الْقَوْمُ إِلَى أَعْمَالِهِمْ فَقَالُوا مُحَمَّدٌ ـ قَالَ عَبْدُ الْعَزِيزِ وَقَالَ بَعْضُ أَصْحَابِنَا ـ وَالْخَمِيسُ‏.‏ يَعْنِي الْجَيْشَ، قَالَ فَأَصَبْنَاهَا عَنْوَةً، فَجُمِعَ السَّبْىُ، فَجَاءَ دِحْيَةُ فَقَالَ يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ، أَعْطِنِي جَارِيَةً مِنَ السَّبْىِ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ اذْهَبْ فَخُذْ جَارِيَةً ‏"‏‏.‏ فَأَخَذَ صَفِيَّةَ بِنْتَ حُيَىٍّ، فَجَاءَ رَجُلٌ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ، أَعْطَيْتَ دِحْيَةَ صَفِيَّةَ بِنْتَ حُيَىٍّ سَيِّدَةَ قُرَيْظَةَ وَالنَّضِيرِ، لاَ تَصْلُحُ إِلاَّ لَكَ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ ادْعُوهُ بِهَا ‏"‏‏.‏ فَجَاءَ بِهَا، فَلَمَّا نَظَرَ

author: Muhammad al-Bukhari (d. 870)
ref: Bukhari 2945 (Book 56 (Jihad), Hadith 157)
arabic: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ مَسْلَمَةَ، عَنْ مَالِكٍ، عَنْ حُمَيْدٍ، عَنْ أَنَسٍ ـ رضى الله عنه أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم خَرَجَ إِلَى خَيْبَرَ فَجَاءَهَا لَيْلاً، وَكَانَ إِذَا جَاءَ قَوْمًا بِلَيْلٍ لاَ يُغِيرُ عَلَيْهِمْ حَتَّى يُصْبِحَ، فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ، خَرَجَتْ يَهُودُ بِمَسَاحِيهِمْ وَمَكَاتِلِهِمْ، فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ قَالُوا مُحَمَّدٌ وَاللَّهِ، مُحَمَّدٌ وَالْخَمِيسُ‏.‏ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، خَرِبَتْ خَيْبَرُ، إِنَّا إِذَا نَزَلْنَا بِسَاحَةِ قَوْمٍ فَسَاءَ صَبَاحُ الْمُنْذَرِينَ ‏"‏‏.‏

(Allah is Greater) and Khaibar is ruined, for whenever we approach a nation (i.e. enemy to fight) then it will be a miserable morning for those who have been warned

The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Khaibar is destroyed, for whenever we approach a (hostile) nation (to fight), then evil will be the morning for those who have been warned

what_it_says: Anas: at dawn at Khaybar, the Jews come out and see the army; the Prophet says 'Khaibar is destroyed' and recites the warned-people line.

work: Sahih al-Bukhari
author: Muhammad al-Bukhari (d. 870)
ref: Bukhari 610 (Book 10 (Adhan), Hadith 8)
arabic: حَدَّثَنَا قُتَيْبَةُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ، عَنْ حُمَيْدٍ، عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانَ إِذَا غَزَا بِنَا قَوْمًا لَمْ يَكُنْ يَغْزُو بِنَا حَتَّى يُصْبِحَ وَيَنْظُرَ، فَإِنْ سَمِعَ أَذَانًا كَفَّ عَنْهُمْ، وَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْمَعْ أَذَانًا أَغَارَ عَلَيْهِمْ، قَالَ فَخَرَجْنَا إِلَى خَيْبَرَ فَانْتَهَيْنَا إِلَيْهِمْ لَيْلاً، فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ وَلَمْ يَسْمَعْ أَذَانًا رَكِبَ وَرَكِبْتُ خَلْفَ أَبِي طَلْحَةَ، وَإِنَّ قَدَمِي لَتَمَسُّ قَدَمَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏ قَالَ فَخَرَجُوا إِلَيْنَا بِمَكَاتِلِهِمْ وَمَسَاحِيهِمْ فَلَمَّا رَأَوُا النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالُوا مُحَمَّدٌ وَاللَّهِ، مُحَمَّدٌ وَالْخَمِيسُ‏.‏ قَالَ فَلَمَّا رَآهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، خَرِبَتْ خَيْبَرُ، إِنَّا إِذَا نَزَلْنَا بِسَاحَةِ قَوْمٍ فَسَاءَ صَبَاحُ الْمُنْذَرِينَ ‏"‏‏.‏
english: Narrated Humaid:Anas bin Malik said, "Whenever the Prophet (ﷺ) went out with us to fight (in Allah's cause) against any nation, he never allowed us to attack till morning and he would wait and see: if he heard Adhan he would postpone the attack and if he did not hear Adhan he would attack them." Anas added, "We reached Khaibar at night and in the morning when he did not hear the Adhan for the prayer, he (the Prophet ) rode and I rode behind Abi Talha and my foot was touching that of the Prophet. The inhabitants of Khaibar came out with their baskets and spades and when they saw the Prophet (ﷺ) they shouted 'Muhammad! By Allah, Muhammad and his army.' When Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) saw them, he said, "Allahu-Akbar! Allahu-Akbar! Khaibar is ruined. Whenever we approach a (hostile) nation (to fight), then evil will be the morning of those who have been warned
translator: not named in the JSON mirror; verify on sunnah.com
what_it_says: Anas: the Prophet did not attack a people before morning; he waited to hear the call to prayer and attacked only if none was heard; at Khaybar, on hearing no adhan, he attacked at dawn.

work: Sirat Rasul Allah / The Life of Muhammad
author: Ibn Ishaq (d. 767), ed. Ibn Hisham
ref: Guillaume p. 515 'The rest of the affair of Khaybar' (Kinana torture); bracketed (764)
english: The apostle gave orders to al-Zubayr b. al-'Awwam, 'Torture him until you extract what he has,' so he kindled a fire with flint and steel on his chest until he was nearly dead. Then the apostle delivered him to Muhammad b. Maslama and he struck off his head, in revenge for his brother Mahmud.
translator: A. Guillaume, The Life of Muhammad (OUP, Karachi; 1955 edition; PDF copy 2010 Adobe scan)
what_it_says: Kinana b. al-Rabi', keeper of the Nadir treasure, is tortured on the Prophet's order to reveal the rest of the treasure and then beheaded by Muhammad b. Maslama.

work: Sirat Rasul Allah / The Life of Muhammad
author: Ibn Ishaq (d. 767), ed. Ibn Hisham
ref: Guillaume pp. 515-516 (Khaybar and Fadak terms); bracketed (765)-(766) region
english: The apostle besieged the people of Khaybar in their two forts al-Wati[h] and al-Sulalim until when they could hold out no longer they asked him to let them go, and spare their lives, and he did so. ... When the people of Fadak heard of what had happened they sent to the apostle asking him to let them go and to spare their lives and they would leave him their property, and he did so. ... When the people of Khaybar surrendered on these conditions they asked the apostle to employ them on the property with half share in the produce ... 'if we wish to expel you we will expel you.'
translator: A. Guillaume, The Life of Muhammad (OUP, Karachi; 1955 edition; PDF copy 2010 Adobe scan)
what_it_says: Khaybar capitulated after a siege and was made to work the land for half the produce on condition of expulsion at will; Fadak surrendered on similar terms.

work: Sirat Rasul Allah / The Life of Muhammad
author: Ibn Ishaq (d. 767), ed. Ibn Hisham
ref: Guillaume p. 576 (Hunayn aftermath: Khalid's killing of a woman); bracketed (856)
english: One of our companions told us that the apostle that day passed by a woman whom Khalid b. al-Walid had killed while men had gathered round her. When he heard what had happened he sent word to Khalid and forbade him to kill child, or woman, or hired slave.
translator: A. Guillaume, The Life of Muhammad (OUP, Karachi; 1955 edition; PDF copy 2010 Adobe scan)
what_it_says: After Hunayn the Prophet rebukes Khalid for killing a woman and forbids killing children, women or hired slaves: a restraint anecdote the sira records.

work: Sirat Rasul Allah / The Life of Muhammad
author: Ibn Ishaq (d. 767), ed. Ibn Hisham
ref: Guillaume p. 587 'The capture of al-Ta'if, A.H. 8'; (catapult sentence)
english: When the fugitives of Thaqif came to al-Ta'if they shut the gates of the city and made preparations for war. Neither 'Urwa b. Mas'ud nor Ghaylan b. Salama were present at Hunayn or at the siege of al-Ta'if; they were in Jurash learning the use of the testudo, the catapult, and other instruments.
translator: A. Guillaume, The Life of Muhammad (OUP, Karachi; 1955 edition; PDF copy 2010 Adobe scan)
page: p. 587 (text layer; header 586 on left half)
what_it_says: Thaqif shut their gates and prepared for war; the sira says two Thaqifite men were in Jurash learning the testudo and catapult (note: the catapult is mentioned on p. 587, not 589).

work: Sirat Rasul Allah / The Life of Muhammad
author: Ibn Ishaq (d. 767), ed. Ibn Hisham
ref: Guillaume p. 589 'siege of al-Ta'if'; bracketed (839), (840); margin 872-873
english: He besieged them for some twenty days (839). ... The apostle besieged them and fought them bitterly and the two sides exchanged arrows (840), until when the day of storming came at the wall of al-Ta'if a number of his Companions went under a testudo and advanced up to the wall to breach it. Thaqif let loose on them scraps of hot iron ... The apostle ordered that the vineyards of Thaqif should be cut down and the men fell upon them cutting them down.
translator: A. Guillaume, The Life of Muhammad (OUP, Karachi; 1955 edition; PDF copy 2010 Adobe scan)
what_it_says: The Prophet besieged al-Ta'if for about twenty days, sent men under a testudo to breach the wall, and ordered the vineyards cut down.

work: Sirat Rasul Allah / The Life of Muhammad
author: Ibn Ishaq (d. 767), ed. Ibn Hisham
ref: Guillaume p. 532 'The expedition to Mu'ta'; bracketed (784)
english: The apostle sent his expedition to Mu'ta in Jumada'l-Ula in the year 8 and put Zayd b. Haritha in command; if Zayd were slain then Jafar b. Abu Talib was to take command, and if he were killed then 'Abdullah b. Rawaha. The expedition got ready to the number of 3,000 ... they heard that Heraclius had come down to Ma'ab in the Balqa' with 100,000 Greeks joined by 100,000 men from Lakhm and Judham ...
translator: A. Guillaume, The Life of Muhammad (OUP, Karachi; 1955 edition; PDF copy 2010 Adobe scan)
what_it_says: In A.H. 8 the Prophet sends about 3,000 men under Zayd b. Haritha toward Syria; on arrival they learn that Heraclius has gathered a force of about 200,000 (Greeks and Arab allies).

work: Sirat Rasul Allah / The Life of Muhammad
author: Ibn Ishaq (d. 767), ed. Ibn Hisham
ref: Guillaume pp. 602-603 'The raid on Tabuk, A.H.9'; bracketed (858), (859)
english: The apostle stayed in Medina from Dhu'l-Hijja to Rajab, and then gave orders to prepare to raid the Byzantines. ... He ordered them to get ready and told them that he was making for the Byzantines. ... the apostle nearly always referred allusively to the destination of a raid ... This was the sole exception, for he said plainly that he was making for the Byzantines because the journey was long, the season difficult, and the enemy in great strength ...
translator: A. Guillaume, The Life of Muhammad (OUP, Karachi; 1955 edition; PDF copy 2010 Adobe scan)
what_it_says: For Tabuk (A.H. 9) the Prophet announced openly that the target was the Byzantines, unlike his usual practice; the sira reports that men were reluctant because of the heat.

work: Sirat Rasul Allah / The Life of Muhammad
author: Ibn Ishaq (d. 767), ed. Ibn Hisham
ref: Guillaume p. 607 'Tabuk' (treaties with Ayla, Jarba' and Adhruh); no bracket number read
english: When the apostle reached Tabuk Yuhanna b. Ru'ba governor of Ayla came and made a treaty with him and paid him the poll tax. The people of Jarba' and Adhruh also came and paid the poll tax. The apostle wrote for them a document which they still have.
translator: A. Guillaume, The Life of Muhammad (OUP, Karachi; 1955 edition; PDF copy 2010 Adobe scan)
page: p. 607 (right half of the spread; 606 on left half)
what_it_says: At Tabuk the governor of Ayla and the people of Jarba' and Adhruh make treaties and pay the poll tax (jizya) to the Prophet.

work: Sirat Rasul Allah / The Life of Muhammad
author: Ibn Ishaq (d. 767), ed. Ibn Hisham
ref: Guillaume p. 608 (Ukaydir of Dumat, poll tax); bracketed (?) on p. 607
english: Then the apostle summoned Khalid b. al-Walid and sent him to Ukaydir at Duma ... It was a summer night with a bright moon and Ukaydir was on the roof ... ...in with them and seized him and killed his brother. ... Then Khalid brought Ukaydir to the apostle who spared his life and made peace with him on condition that he paid the poll tax. Then he released him and he returned to his town.
translator: A. Guillaume, The Life of Muhammad (OUP, Karachi; 1955 edition; PDF copy 2010 Adobe scan)
page: pp. 607-608 (p. 607 right half: raid on Ukaydir; p. 608 left half: poll-tax peace)
what_it_says: Khalid captures Ukaydir (Christian ruler of Dumat) at night, kills his brother; Ukaydir is then spared on condition he pays the poll tax (jizya).

work: Sirat Rasul Allah / The Life of Muhammad
author: Ibn Ishaq (d. 767), ed. Ibn Hisham
ref: Guillaume p. 620 (Ibn Ishaq's commentary quoting Q 9:29, Guillaume's translation)
english: 'Fight those who do not believe in God and the last day and forbid not that which God and His apostle have forbidden and follow not the religion of truth from among those who have been given the scripture until they pay ... the poll tax out of hand being humbled,' i.e. as a compensation for what you fear to lose by the closing of the markets.
translator: A. Guillaume, The Life of Muhammad (OUP, Karachi; 1955 edition; PDF copy 2010 Adobe scan)
what_it_says: The sira's commentary on Tabuk-era Sura 9 quotes the jizya verse (9:29) and explains it as compensation for the loss of pilgrim trade.

work: Qur'an
author: (revelation; Medina period)
arabic: قَٰتِلُوا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَلَا بِٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ وَلَا يُحَرِّمُونَ مَا حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَلَا يَدِينُونَ دِينَ ٱلْحَقِّ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ حَتَّىٰ يُعْطُوا۟ ٱلْجِزْيَةَ عَن يَدٍۢ وَهُمْ صَٰغِرُونَ
english: Fight those who do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day and who do not consider unlawful what Allah and His Messenger have made unlawful and who do not adopt the religion of truth from those who were given the Scripture - [fight] until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled.
translator: Sahih International (en.sahih, via alquran.cloud)
what_it_says: Fight those who do not believe ... until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled.

work: Qur'an
author: (revelation; Medina period)
arabic: وَأَنزَلَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَٰهَرُوهُم مِّنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ مِن صَيَاصِيهِمْ وَقَذَفَ فِى قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلرُّعْبَ فَرِيقًۭا تَقْتُلُونَ وَتَأْسِرُونَ فَرِيقًۭا وَأَوْرَثَكُمْ أَرْضَهُمْ وَدِيَٰرَهُمْ وَأَمْوَٰلَهُمْ وَأَرْضًۭا لَّمْ تَطَـُٔوهَا ۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ قَدِيرًۭا
english: And He brought down those who supported them among the People of the Scripture from their fortresses and cast terror into their hearts [so that] a party you killed, and you took captive a party. And He caused you to inherit their land and their homes and their properties and a land which you have not trodden. And ever is Allah, over all things, competent.
translator: Sahih International (en.sahih, via alquran.cloud)
what_it_says: Allah brought down the Qurayza's allies from their fortresses, cast terror into their hearts, and gave the Muslims their land: 'a party you killed, and you took captive a party'.

work: Sirat Rasul Allah / The Life of Muhammad
author: Ibn Ishaq (d. 767), ed. Ibn Hisham
ref: Guillaume p. 449 'The raid on Dumatu'l-Jandal, A.H.5' (bracketed (695))
english: The apostle returned to Medina and stayed there some months until Dhu'l-Hijja had passed. This was the fourth year of his sojourn in Medina ... Then he raided Dumatu'l-Jandal (695). Then he returned, not having reached the place, without fighting, and stayed in Medina for the rest of the year.
translator: A. Guillaume, The Life of Muhammad (OUP, Karachi; 1955 edition; PDF copy 2010 Adobe scan)
what_it_says: A.H. 5 raid on Dumat al-Jandal: the Prophet set out, did not reach the place and returned without fighting (the sira counts it among the raids).

work: Sirat Rasul Allah / The Life of Muhammad
author: Ibn Ishaq (d. 767), ed. Ibn Hisham
ref: Guillaume p. 659 'A summary of the apostle's fights' (with (T. six) variant)
english: A SUMMARY OF THE APOSTLE'S FIGHTS. The apostle took part personally in twenty-seven (T. six) raids: Waddan which was the raid of al-Abwa' ... Buwat in the direction of Radwa ... Ushayra in the valley of Yanbu' ... The first fight at Badr in pursuit of Kurz b. Jabir ... Banu Nadir ... Dhatu'l-Riqa' of Nakhl ... The last battle of Badr ... Dumatu'l-Jandal ... [continues on p. 660: al-Khandaq, Banu Qurayza, Banu Lihyan of Hudhayl, Dhu Qarad, Banu'l-Mustaliq of Khuza'a, al-Hudaybiya, Khaybar, the occupation of Mecca, Hunayn, al-Ta'if, Tabuk]. [Footnote] I.H. has counted the pilgrimage as a raid.
translator: A. Guillaume, The Life of Muhammad (OUP, Karachi; 1955 edition; PDF copy 2010 Adobe scan)
what_it_says: Ibn Ishaq's own summary lists the raids he took part in personally (27, with Tabari reading 'six'); the list runs from al-Abwa' to Tabuk and the footnote says Ibn Hisham counted the pilgrimage as a raid.

work: Sirat Rasul Allah / The Life of Muhammad
author: Ibn Ishaq (d. 767), ed. Ibn Hisham
ref: Guillaume p. 660 'Summary of the expeditions and raiding parties' and 'He actually fought in nine engagements'
english: A SUMMARY OF THE EXPEDITIONS AND RAIDING PARTIES. These were thirty-eight (T. thirty-five) in number (T. between the time of his coming to Medina and his death). ... He actually fought in nine engagements: Badr; Uhud; al-Khandaq; Qurayza; al-Mustaliq; Khaybar; the occupation; Hunayn; and al-Ta'if.
translator: A. Guillaume, The Life of Muhammad (OUP, Karachi; 1955 edition; PDF copy 2010 Adobe scan)
what_it_says: Ibn Ishaq counts 38 expeditions and raiding parties sent out (Tabari: 35) and says the Prophet actually fought in nine engagements, a number that matches Ibn Sa'd's nine.

work: Kitab al-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. 2 Part 1, section 1 (Account of the number of the Ghazwahs and Sariyyahs)
author: Muhammad Ibn Sa'd (d. 845)
ref: Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat vol. 2 pt. 1, section 1 (text page marker [P. 2])
english: The number of the ghazwahs of the Apostle of Allah, may Allah bless him, which he conducted personally, was twenty-seven, and (the number of) the suriyyahs which he despatched was forty-seven. In nine ghazwahs he took part in (actual) fighting. They were: (1) al-Badr al-qital, (2) Uhud, (3) al-Muraysi', (4) al-Khandaq, (5) Qurayzah, (6) Khaybar, (7) the Victory of Makkah, (8) Hunayn, and (9) al-Ta'if. The consensus of opinion has been on this number. According to some of their narrations he also fought in the battle of Banu al-Nadir ...
translator: not named on the page; the 1967 Pakistan Historical Society vol. 2 translation is the likely source (UNCONFIRMED)
what_it_says: Ibn Sa'd's own count: 27 ghazwahs the Prophet led personally, 47 sariyyahs he sent out, and nine ghazwahs with fighting (his list differs from Ibn Ishaq's: al-Muraysi' for al-Mustaliq).

work: Sahih al-Bukhari
author: Muhammad al-Bukhari (d. 870)
ref: Bukhari 3949 (Book 64 (Maghazi), Hadith 1)
arabic: حَدَّثَنِي عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، حَدَّثَنَا وَهْبٌ، حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، كُنْتُ إِلَى جَنْبِ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَرْقَمَ، فَقِيلَ لَهُ كَمْ غَزَا النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم مِنْ غَزْوَةٍ قَالَ تِسْعَ عَشْرَةَ‏.‏ قِيلَ كَمْ غَزَوْتَ أَنْتَ مَعَهُ قَالَ سَبْعَ عَشْرَةَ‏.‏ قُلْتُ فَأَيُّهُمْ كَانَتْ أَوَّلَ قَالَ الْعُسَيْرَةُ أَوِ الْعُشَيْرُ‏.‏ فَذَكَرْتُ لِقَتَادَةَ فَقَالَ الْعُشَيْرُ‏.‏
english: Narrated Abu 'Is-haq:Once, while I was sitting beside Zaid bin Al-Arqam, he was asked, "How many Ghazwat did the Prophet undertake?" Zaid replied, "Nineteen." They said, "In how many Ghazwat did you join him?" He replied, "Seventeen." I asked, "Which of these was the first?" He replied, "Al-`Ashira or Al- `Ashiru
translator: not named in the JSON mirror; verify on sunnah.com
what_it_says: Zayd b. Arqam: the Prophet undertook nineteen ghazwat; Zayd himself joined seventeen, and the first was al-'Usayra or al-'Ushayr.
